contact_edits.before: Jennifer H. Capraru, the director, clearly lays out the play's emotional geography but runs into problems, probably not of her own making, with the physical. A site-specific production raises high expectations of scenic realism; otherwise, why not set the play on a conventional stage? Here we have a living-room that changes without warning into a bedroom, and a basement that seems to be on the same level as the rest of the house. When you stop believing in a play's spatial dynamic, you start having problems with its character dynamics as well. This aside, the design is excellent; as might be expected, since it's by Tamara Marie Kucheran, who's also responsible for the Passe Muraille revival of The Drawer Boy and, last year at Stratford, for the gorgeous Fanny Kemble. The play's title is a poser; it doesn't acquire any relevance until the play is almost over, and it seems arbitrary and sentimental when it does. But it isn't quite the end; and when Ferry's Kenny shuffles off into the night, leaving chaos behind him, he moves you not as a figure on a sociologist's graph, but as a complex, inexplicable human being. - Performances run through Nov. 18. For tickets, call 416-460-9306.
